scope: Real subscription operation and truthful progress on synthetic fixtures; not a recall benchmark or a GitHub comment-delivery test

regression.change: Four-file paginated document export; owner scoping lost on continuation pages
regression.head: 85555a00cc712917ee74a6f2b25da68207fcd583

blockers.title: Export pages after the first omit ownerId and return other users' documents
blockers.reason: When a user has more documents than one page holds, later pages call `repository.listDocuments({ cursor: page.nextCursor })` without `ownerId`. The repository treats a missing `ownerId` as a query over all owners (`src/repositories/documents.mjs:4-6`). The export then leaks other users' document ids, titles and dates. It can also skip or duplicate the user's own documents, because the cursor is an offset into the owner-filtered list but is applied to the unfiltered one.
blockers.fix: Keep the owner scope on every page. Build the query once from `{ ownerId: userId }` and call `repository.listDocuments({ ownerId: userId, cursor: page.nextCursor })` for later pages, or run one loop with `cursor` starting as `undefined`.
blockers.validation: Use a repository with page size 2 and documents [a1(u1), b1(u2), a2(u1), b2(u2), a3(u1)]. `handleExport({ id: 'u1' }, repo)` should return exactly ['a1','a2','a3'] with `count` 3 and no u2 documents. The current code returns ['a1','a2','a2','b2','a3'].

limits: Fixtures are deliberately seeded and synthetic
Progress metadata omits raw errors and model/source text
Large-change routing, incremental re-review and live GitHub delivery not qualified by these runs
